subject: Acme - SLO/SLA language and latency measurement clarifications
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Leah Barnes <leah.barnes@acme.com>, Tom Chen <tom.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T10:15:00Z
Subject: Acme - follow-up: performance SLOs & SLA language

Thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps from Redwood:

- Target latency: you mentioned p95 <= 250ms for single-turn text generation (50 token outputs) and streaming experience for longer responses with token-level streaming within ~50ms per token after first token.
- Throughput/concurrency: expected steady-state throughput ~600 requests/min with spikes to 1,500 req/min; concurrency target 200 concurrent requests.
- Measurement: you asked whether latency is measured server-side or end-to-end (including client decode). We usually define latency as server-side request-to-last-byte-send (server egress), measured at the edge for the customer region. Cold start exclusion and retry/backoff behavior are typical exclusions—see attached draft.
- SLA language: you asked about remedies. Our standard offering is uptime SLA with credit tiers; for performance SLOs we offer monthly reporting, 99% p95 compliance target with rolling windows and customer alerts; remedies are credits tiered by monthly impact.

Attached is an initial SLO/SLA draft and a short appendix on measurement definitions. Rafael, can you confirm the streaming measurement approach and any important exclusions to call out? Leah/Tom—can you confirm whether p95 at server-egress is acceptable or you need client-end-to-end measurements?

Next steps:
1) Redwood to share SLO draft (attached)  — Marissa (today)
2) Acme to confirm measurement point and exclusions  — Leah/Tom (by 2026-07-22)
3) If acceptable, legal/procurement to circulate procurement/DocuSign  — target week of 2026-07-27

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Leah Barnes <leah.barnes@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Chen <tom.chen@acme.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T14:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Acme - follow-up: performance SLOs & SLA language

Thanks Marissa — that recap is helpful. A couple clarifications from our side:

- p95 <= 250ms acceptable if measured server-side (server egress). We do want a separate client-end measurement for the UI team but that can be tracked independently.
- For streaming: need to ensure first token latency <= 300ms and subsequent token latency <= 60ms for 95% of tokens during steady-state. Can you confirm how you measure token latency (network+server vs server-only)?
- Exclusions: we need explicit language around DDoS and provider-initiated maintenance windows. Also want to understand how retries and queued requests are treated for concurrency measurements.

Also, procurement will want the exact credit table for SLO misses (percentage of monthly bill). Please include that in the SLA draft.

-Leah

On a related note, can Rafael loop in any suggested config (batch sizes, concurrency limits) that help hit these numbers?

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Leah Barnes <leah.barnes@acme.com>, Tom Chen <tom.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T16:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Acme - follow-up: performance SLOs & SLA language

Hi all — quick technical notes:

- Latency measurement: for contractual SLOs we recommend server-side p95 measured at the regional edge (time from request accept on edge to last byte sent to client). This avoids client-side variability. For streaming token latency we measure server-side token emit time delta. Network jitter is an operational factor but not part of the contractual metric.
- Cold starts: exclude requests that experience a model instance cold start (>500ms extra) for the first N minutes after scaling events; define a 5-minute stabilization window after auto-scale movements.
- Retries: treat retries as part of the original request if automatic retry within K seconds; manual retries count separately. We'll include explicit retry handling language.
- Concurrency: define concurrency as simultaneous active requests in the serving pool; queued requests waiting in the ingress queue are excluded from active concurrency but included in latency calculations if they contribute to total response time.
- Config suggestions: for your throughput targets we'd recommend initial dedicated capacity of 4 GPU workers with batching target ~32 requests/batch and max concurrency 250, plus KV caching for repeated prompts. We'll provide a config appendix.

I'll update the SLO appendix and include the credit table options (0.5%/1%/2% monthly bill tiers depending on severity) and circulate a revised PDF by EOD.

-Rafael

Attachment references: latency_measurement_appendix.xlsx

- Reporting cadence: monthly automated report, near-real-time dashboard access, weekly executive summary on request
- Remedies: tiered service credits table and escalation path (SRE-to-SRE, AEs notified)

Leah/Tom — can you confirm by 2026-07-23 whether the definitions and credit table look acceptable? If so, I'll loop in procurement/legal and push a DocuSign in the week of 2026-07-27.
